score_reason: Useful consumer protection announced by Google, but claims are untested and the rollout is still weeks away.
headline: Google is adding an opt-in Gemini-powered check to Google Messages that judges whether unknown senders are trying to scam you.
importance_line: Android users, many of whom face scam texts, get a stronger optional defence, though it sends message content to the cloud and Google's effectiveness claims are untested.
summary: The Verge reports that Google is rolling out an opt-in 'enhanced protection' mode in Google Messages in the coming weeks, which uses cloud-based Gemini AI to assess what an unrecognised sender is after, and Google says the data is encrypted and kept in a secure space. Google is also blocking apps from setting up call forwarding and extending scam detection for chat notifications from Pixel phones to phones from brands including Xiaomi, Oppo, OnePlus and Motorola.
notes: Read full text from The Verge.
